input.title: Is this the end for ‘encro’ phones?
input.abstract: Encrypted, or ‘encro’, phones are the communication method of choice for organised crime groups (OCGs) across the UK and Europe. Until 2020, the encro was seen as a completely secure and anonymous way of organised criminal groups contacting each other without fear of detection or tracing. However, the apparent ‘hack’ of one encro phone operator and the compromise of a number of devices, followed by multiple arrests, suggest that the previously airtight encro phones are not as reliable as users once thought, explains Catherine O'Rourke at JMW. Encrypted phones, or ‘encro’ phones, are the communication method of choice for organised crime groups (OCGs) across the UK and Europe, because of their apparent entirely secure features. Encro phones were originally designed for military use, but more recently, they have been associated with celebrities wishing to secure their privacy, and for criminal activity. © 2020 Elsevier Ltd
